none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Constrained monotone variational inequality: find an approximate zero of F+N_X. The feasible set X is nonempty, compact and convex, with diameter at most D and x0∈X. F need not be a gradient or arise from a saddle-point objective.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Two separately counted exact oracles return F(x) and the full Fréchet derivative DF(x). Replies are exact for every query, history and seed. All Params, including X, x0, L, D, ε and m, are public; F is hidden. No stochastic or inexact oracle error is present.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/LipschitzJacobianMonotone.lean: spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.Reply, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm; no dimension bound is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: F is differentiable at every point of X, monotone on X, and satisfies ‖DF(x)−DF(y)‖≤L‖x−y‖ on X. No bound on ‖DF(x)‖ is supplied. L,D,ε>0 and the public integer m≥1; m imposes no structural restriction on F.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned point must belong to X exactly.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the residual bound must hold almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within fixed separate oracle budgets.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The output x must admit n∈N_X(x) with ‖F(x)+n‖≤ε, where N_X(x)={n: ⟨n,z−x⟩≤0 for every z∈X}. This is an unsquared tangent-residual norm criterion.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: A standard smooth monotone variational inequality on a compact convex set, with exact operator/Jacobian access and a normal-cone residual accuracy criterion. Separate oracle accounting does not change the underlying formulation.
